text:
marta: FYI we got an escalation from customer acme-inc — sudden p99 generator latency jump ~120ms -> ~2.3s starting ~08:15 UTC. They say requests are being routed through eu-west despite region hinting to us. Can infra look?

sam: On it. Do we have a sample trace or request-id from the customer?

marta: They attached trace id: trace:acme-9843. Also pasted their traceroute showing a hop through bdr-edge01.eu-west-1: 

```
> traceroute to api.redwood.example (54.34.12.8), 30 hops max
> 1  10.0.0.1  0.7 ms
> 7  bdr-edge01.eu-west-1  120.8 ms
> 8  sfo-proxy01.us-west-1  2.1 ms
```

marta: They said their SDK sets region: us-west-1 and sends header `X-Client-Region: us-west-1`.

sam: Hmm. Could be an edge egress selection fallback — maybe the edge lost local capacity and fell back to bdr-edge. Need router traces for that timeframe. Jun, can you pull routing decisions for tenant acme-inc between 08:10-08:20 UTC?

jun: Pulling now. I see a handful of routed requests that hit edge-group-us-west then got rewritten via egress-mapper to eu-egress-01 for about 5m. Logs show this bit: `egress_decision: FALLBACK_CAPACITY:eu-variant` for route /v1/generate.

sam: Can you paste the short log snippet?

jun: Copied: 

```
[08:14:22Z] tenant=acme-inc route=/v1/generate model=rw-13b seq=64 region_hint=us-west-1 available_local=0 fallback_policy=allow_eu
[08:14:22Z] egress_decision: FALLBACK_CAPACITY -> egress=eu-variant host=bdr-edge01.eu-west-1
```

sam: That explains the hop. Why would available_local=0 be reported? Are the us-west pools saturated or marked unhealthy?

oliver: I checked Dedicated capacity for that account — no reserved capacity there. For Hosted, we had a short autoscaler cooldown around 08:13 due to a transient metric spike; scaling didn't add new instances fast enough. The routing policy allows egress fallbacks to keep requests served.

marta: Customer is upset because they have latency SLO tied to region affinity. They expected a hard-pin to us-west. Can we show them the exact routing events and propose mitigation?

sam: Short-term: we can enable a tenant-specific routing override to prefer local-only until traffic subsides. Will need ops signoff. Medium-term: adjust cooldown / add a soft-capacity buffer for region-affinity customers.

jun: For repro steps I asked the customer to run a quick curl that forces a server-side route decision and capture server decision header:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
# look for X-Redwood-Route and X-Redwood-Egress headers
```

marta: Customer returned this header dump: 

```
X-Redwood-Route: /v1/generate
X-Redwood-Region-Decision: egress=eu-variant fallback_reason=capacity
X-Request-Id: trace:acme-9843
```

marta: They also included timing: client->edge 30ms, edge->eu 2300ms roundtrip.

sam: Ok. Action items: 
- Jun: collect routing decision logs for tenant (08:10-08:20) — prioritize entries with fallback_reason=capacity.
- Oliver: confirm autoscaler cooldown and whether we hit any provision limits in us-west at that time.
- Marta: share proposed short-term override with customer and offer credit for SLO miss.

jun: Got the logs — filing a trace bundle. Also saw one noisier metric from our prefix cache (`kv-cache-hit` temporarily dropped) that coincided with the spike; may have increased load on serving hosts.

oliver: Confirmed: at 08:12 our autoscaler saw a rapid spike and entered cooldown due to concurrent scale jobs; we were briefly underprovisioned by ~18% for that model profile. No hard failures, just load shedding to fallbacks.

marta: Customer asked whether this is a one-off or systemic. Any chance of config that treats region_hint as a hard pin?

sam: We do support tenant-pinning but it's opt-in; default is soft affinity to improve availability. We can enable hard pin for them but that increases chance of 5xx if local capacity is exhausted. I'll draft the options and risk matrix.

deploy-bot: [deploy] autoscaler/fixes/soft-affinity-bump scheduled to canary in us-west at 10:00 UTC.

marta: Good. I'll route a short RCA to the customer: explain the fallback policy, show logs, offer a credit, and propose either a hard-pin or reserved capacity.

jun: For long-term: recommend adding a tiny standby pool for region-affinity high-SLO tenants; also add trace header `X-Redwood-Egress` to SDK responses so customer trace matches server decision.

sam: Agreed. Closing loop once canary passes and after we send customer update. :thumbsup:

marta: Thanks team. I'll attach the trace bundle to the ticket and mark this thread for follow-up.
